수백년 전 과거에 인간들을 다스리던 타이탄. 백년 전에 프로메테우스가 죽고, 왕좌의 공석을 둘러싸고 타이탄들끼리 전쟁이 일어나, 수많은 인명피해와 타이탄들이 쓰러지고 세계가 멸망할 뻔했다. 그렇게 전쟁은 멈췄지만 아직 남은 타이탄들이 다시 한번 전쟁을 준비해, 이를 막기 위해 'Furies'(퓨리즈) 라는 4명의 여성으로 이루어진 팀이 움직이는 것이 게임의 스토리.

벨트스크롤 액션 게임 + RPG 적인 요소가 혼합, 몹을 사냥하거나 스테이지를 클리어 하면 얻게 되는 골드 등으로 캐릭터들을 강화시키는 것이 주이다. 플레이 가능한 캐릭터는 4명이며 우선 팀의 리더이자 '탱커' 포지션의 'Triss'(트리스), 팀의 '두뇌' 담당이며 '엔지니어' 포지션의 'Erin'(에린), 단순무식하고 저돌적이지만 착하고 예의바른 '전사' 포지션의 'Alex'(알렉스), 팀의 척후이자 '저격수' 포지션이며 캐릭터 중 난이도가 가장 높은 'Meg'(메그) 가 있다.

싱글 플레이 시에는 혼자 2명의 캐릭터를 바꿔가며 사용해야 하고 멀티 시에는 최대 4인이서 플레이 가능하고 각각 하나의 캐릭터로 게임을 진행하게 된다. 싱글이든 멀티든 각자의 역할이 명확하기에 협력하지 않으면 진행이 어려운 구조로 되어있다.

조작 자체는 기본적인 액션 구조를 따르기에 비교적 직관적이다. 공격, 회피, 스킬, 적마다의 패턴과 속성, 연계와 타이밍 등이 팀 전체의 협력과 혼자 플레이 시에 캐릭터의 빠른 전환에 재미를 더해준다.

그래픽은 카툰 스타일의 2D 아트를 사용해서 전체적으로 밝고 유쾌한 분위기를 유지한다. 사운드도 경쾌한 느낌으로 게임의 빠른 템포와 어울린다.

협동 게임이고 출시한지 시간이 꽤 흘러서 온라인에 사람들이 보이지 않아서 준비물로 가장 어려운 '친구' 가 필요하다. 그러나 멀티 만큼의 재미는 못 미치지만 싱글 플레이의 매력도 있으니 할인 할 때 구매하여 즐겨보는 것도 나쁘지 않을 것 같습니다. (그래도 혼자서는 도저히 재미 없다 하시는 분들은 친추나 댓글로 함께 하자고 말씀을 하신다면 참여해보도록 하겠습니다.)

It is a fun brawler and bullet-hell combination game with a nice visual aesthetic, but held back by some unfortunate design decisions that make it less fun to play in offline or solo mode, as the online play in 2025 is mostly dead.

The color-specific shielding mechanic for enemies is an interesting gimmick for a while and is probably a good way to encourage team play in online or local multiplayer matches, but in solo mode it feels like an unnecessary chore to constantly switch back and forth between party members. 

Additionally, the 4 active abilities for each character have up to 3 other unlockable variations each. It does add some depth and much-needed variety to the combat, but some of the skills are unlocked so late in the game that they don't really add any fun or variety until the combat has gotten stale.

It is a fun and somewhat unique brawler/bullet hell mash-up to check out, but fans of either genre may find better options elsewhere.

This game is a gem. A beat em up with pretty interesting mechanics. It can be hit and miss, but to me a lot of the unique mechanics are good hits.
I'll have to say though it's better played as a playthrough game, something you play and progress through together with the same people, and not treated as a party game where people just play for a session and be done with it. That said, the game isn't that long, you can beat the game within 20 hours.
The game also has very good online coop implementation, it's pretty smooth and i only encountered a few minor bugs (which only happens when someone is really laggy)

In my opinion, despite the genre, this game is also more fitting for RPG players or at least gamers that can appreciate the puzzle aspect, especially better if you can discuss it with friends. The riddle/puzzles aren't easy at all and requires some thinking, especially the first one since you don't always expect puzzles from games of this genre to need out of the box thinking.

Difficulty wise it's generally pretty fair, a lot of the bosses aren't really that difficult but they generally have adds and that tests your ability to keep track of multiple different attacks and prioritizing some targets. There are some significant difficulty spikes here and there though, could've been smoother, but nothing too unmanageable. The game itself is also pretty generous and you keep the money/mastery you get even from failed runs (and each transitions/waves generally give you money rewards), so retrying a stage doesn't really feel bad at all.

Solid pick especially for online co-op.

Le truc que vous remarquerez le plus vite, c'est que faire des trickshot à plusieurs c'est [i]extrêmement[/i] marrant et que vous allez [i]tout le temps[/i] vouloir en faire.

C'est un jeu vraiment nerveux ; des fois t'as des mobs sur la totalité de l'écran, faut esquiver une tonne de projectiles et de coups de mêlée -- et pendant ce temps tu vises les mobs tout en comptant les secondes avant de pouvoir réutiliser ton ulti... Quand le combat se joue à un cheveu et que ça finit par passer, c'est la meilleure sensation au monde. C'est tellement satisfaisant.

Le seul truc qu'on n'a pas aimé faire, c'est la quête pour la True Ending parce qu'elle est tellement bien cachée qu'on s'est très vite tourné vers un guide (et même comme ça c'était long de faire les allers-retour)
Aussi et malheureusement le jeu n'est pas cross-plateforme : par exemple si l'un de vous est sur SteamDeck pendant qu'un autre est sur Windows, vous serez complètement désynchronisés au point que vous ne pourrez pas jouer ! Il faut obligatoirement que vous jouiez tous sur la même plateforme (Linux, Windows ou Mac)

This game is a real gem that went completely unnoticed.
Extremely fun and satisfying co-op beat 'em up with 4 completely different characters you can chose from (looking at you Castle Crashers, with your 50 copy-pasted playable characters), each with their unique tech tree and equipments, that you can mix and match to change completely the way you play the character.
The game also encourages the player to change equipment, by giving small stats increase, this way you are more incentivized to experiment and not stick to the same build for the entire game.

Many people dislike the colored shields that the enemies get, that must be destroyed by a specific character. I find this mechanic perfect for single player, so you are forced to swap characters, and it also works great in two players. I imagine that if you are in 4 players and the enemies keep changing shield color it can be become annoying tho. (There is a mod to remove the shields if you don't like them).

A negative thing for pretty much anyone are rosetta stones, the "riddles" you have to complete to get the true ending. This was truly an incredible gem of a game, a fine blend of an arcade-y beat-'em-up, fun writing and exceptionally clever puzzles. I played it with three friends and enjoyed an unparalleled experience - and I mean that. There are truly so few games out there doing what Full Metal Furies does with its puzzles, from their depth to their creativity to their meta-construction, right down to the incredibly fine line walked by the developers as they threaded clues and directions that wouldn't give away too much. And I greatly loved the four distinct classes, further specialized with the gear choices and the skill trees that add a wonderful sense of both progression and personalization.

I'd be remiss to not mention the gorgeous visuals and wonderful soundtrack as well. The spritework is incredible! The game is bursting with personality and fine details that build such a wonderful, breathtaking world. And I'll forever be a fan of including silly interactables like petting Go-Cat and playing the musical instruments - little things that just make the world feel a touch more alive.

The feelings of triumph and satisfaction my friends and I shared as all four of us worked together to pool our unique ideas and perspectives into slowly cracking these puzzles is something I'll hold on to for a long time. Huge respect to the developers for taking a chance on making something like this. And if they still have the ideas and drive to do it, I sincerely hope they take a crack at a sequel one day; I'll always be a fan of developers carving out new paths with wholly new games, but there are simply so few games like this that I can't help but want more!

Even if we don't get a sequel though, this game will forever be something special.
